referents.why: The possessive 'their' is masculine plural and modifies 'secret arts' (w6). The only agreeing masculine plural in this verse is the magicians (w4), and the enchantments are theirs.
Implied third masculine plural subject of the wayyiqtol 'brought up'. Frogs (w12) are feminine and cannot be the doers. The subject is the same magicians as in cl0.
referents.category: implied subject carried over within the verse

links.why: The builder's cl2 is the last clause of the previous verse (Exo.8.2#cl2, it covered the land of Egypt), not a clause of this verse. The then type is within a verse only; across verses is the episode rung, which link_types does not supply.
The second clause is a wayyiqtol with fused waw that continues the narrative line of the first within the verse.

The magicians did thus (ken) as Aaron had just stretched out his hand (8:2). Their subject is named (the magicians, w4) and they were not commanded to do it, so this is imitation, not fulfilment. Aaron's own act carried out the command of 8:1.
The clause gives the content of what the magicians did as cl0 reports it: they brought the frogs up onto the land of Egypt.

groups.why: Two clauses in a row are acts of one agent, the magicians. Each states its subject only in its verb, and both point to w4.

none_fit.what: Narrative continuation across a verse boundary (the episode rung). link_types allows then only within a verse, so the builder's cross-verse link has no permitted type.
